summary.plain: The smaller, more tightly packed of the two KM3NeT telescopes, built to study neutrinos made in Earth's atmosphere and work out how the three kinds of neutrino are ordered by mass. It sits 2450 metres down on the seabed off Toulon, France.
summary.technical: KM3NeT/ORCA (Oscillation Research with Cosmics in the Abyss): sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope at the KM3NeT-Fr site off Toulon, France (2450 m depth), designed as one building block of 115 detection units (~7 Mt instrumented seawater) for atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements and neutrino mass ordering; 42 detection units were installed as of July 2026, with construction ongoing.

technology.quote: One building block will be configured to precisely measure atmospheric neutrino oscillations.
technology.value: Sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: vertical strings of digital optical modules with closer sensor spacing than ARCA, optimised for lower-energy atmospheric neutrinos
